name: Finland
sources: GDP about $139bn and population 4.99m (World Bank / Tilastokeskus, 1990).
Inflation 6.1% (Tilastokeskus consumer price index, 1990). Bank of Finland base rate 8.5% but HELIBOR ran near 14% as the markka's peg came under pressure; 14% is the market rate the model needs.
Tax revenue 43% of GDP (OECD Revenue Statistics, 1990). General government debt only 14% of GDP in 1990 - the lowest on this roster - before the 1991-93 depression took it past 55%.
Defence 1.6% of GDP. Strength 8 covers a territorial defence system with a wartime strength above 500,000 under universal conscription, constrained by the 1947 Paris peace treaty ceilings.

Authoritarianism 0.10 rather than the 0.07 of the other Nordics: Finland is a full democracy, but the 1948 Treaty of Friendship, Cooperation and Mutual Assistance with the Soviet Union constrained foreign policy and, through self-censorship, domestic debate. The treaty lapsed with the USSR in 1991.
Finland's bilateral clearing trade with the Soviet Union was about a fifth of exports and collapsed in 1991; the model reaches the depression through that channel rather than by script.
